description: ISO/IEC 24745 and ISO/IEC 30136 Claim Restatement and Threat Model
s3_claims_quoted: Keyed orthogonal rotation R in O(d) provides ISO/IEC 24745 irreversibility and unlinkability by transforming templates prior to storage.
AES-256-GCM envelope encryption provides cryptographic confidentiality at rest with crypto-shredding on account deletion.

irreversibility.rationale: An orthogonal rotation is an isometry. Given k=128 known public face pairs, Orthogonal Procrustes recovers R exactly, rendering rotation reversible.

unlinkability.rationale: Because rotations preserve inner products identically, pairwise Gram similarity matrices match across tenants with Gomez-Barrero D_lr = 1.0.

renewability.rationale: Drawing a new rotation matrix R' changes stored vectors, but an attacker with historical templates can cross-link them via distance preservation.

true_production_security.rationale: Strong semantic security under IND-CCA2. Individual ephemeral per-user data keys crypto-shredded upon DPDPA erasure request.

held_assets: Full database dump of rotated embeddings
SFace ONNX model weights and architecture (public open-source)
High-resolution public photos of target subjects (e.g. social media, company directories)
Full database dump of a partner tenant system
attacker_model.capabilities: Known-Plaintext Attack (KPA) using Orthogonal Procrustes; Cross-tenant Gram matrix isomorphism linkage.
